title: Your street comes to life
summary: Walk your neighborhood in Street view, design your yard in the new Your Streetview editor, and watch neighbors and lights bring the city to life.
changes: Added Street view. Drag the little person onto a highlighted street, or select it and choose a street, to explore the city in first person.
Added Your Streetview, a top-down editor opened from your tower layers. Pick a 3D model from the shelf to preview it, snap it to your plot's grid, rotate it, and place it without leaving the editor.
Spend bricks on flower planters, benches, lamps, small trees, sculptures, neighbors, and corner shops. Level 4 towers can add storefronts that sit flush against the building's walls.
Pick up your own items in Street view, walk them somewhere new, and set them down again. Moving items you already own is free.
Neighbors you buy now stroll to nearby shops and head back home, walking around buildings and furnishings.
The city follows your local time of day. Lamps and shop windows warmly light the sidewalks in the evening, and lighting stays steady while you pan.
Wild woodland now grows around undeveloped land beyond the city's edge.
A new neighborhood guide spotlights real controls and moves forward as you open the editor, place your first item, and start a walk. Skip it anytime or replay it from Settings.
The city draws faster and more smoothly as it grows, and recovers if your graphics context is interrupted.
Purchases interrupted by a lost connection now finish safely, without charging twice or losing the item's placement.

title: Build the city together
summary: Open-source contributions now earn XP, Makers square has a richer construction plan, and mobile invitations reopen smoothly.
changes: Approved pull requests merged into C.I.T.I.E.S now award 100 XP to the linked resident, once per contribution.
Rebuilt Makers square with patterned paving, planted wings, benches, lighting, worktables, staged materials, a canopy, and a landmark sculpture.
Made the square follow its irregular parcel and simplify cleanly when viewing the city from farther away.
Fixed the mobile invitation pane so reopening it returns to the expected position instead of jumping.
Refocused the open-source project guide on the core loop, XP, major mechanics, contribution rewards, and a real city view.

title: A smoother city on mobile
summary: Navigation, customization, and onboarding now fit smaller screens more comfortably.
changes: Added Changelog beside the city logo. Open it to see past updates in a panel that slides down from the top; use the bottom arrow to tuck it away.
Made tower and project sheets, theme cards, text, and tap targets easier to use on phones. Closed panels no longer leave hidden controls in the keyboard navigation.
Improved small-screen and landscape layouts for invitations, profile editing, and plot placement. Invitation links stay readable, and the location selection controls fit on screen.
Added a visible close button to mobile search, kept the city logo visible while searching, and improved navigation through search results.
Fixed mobile onboarding spotlights to point at the bottom navigation controls and visible tower layers. Guide bubbles now stay within the screen, including after resizing.
Improved mobile map framing and prevented drags and multi-touch gestures from accidentally selecting a tower or plot.
Adjusted panels and inputs for the on-screen keyboard, and made opening another panel close conflicting navigation views.
Corrected the GitHub reward help text to show the existing daily limit of 200 XP and 200 bricks.
